subject: humanities
passage: Publishers often assume that listeners give up on long audiobooks more readily than readers give up on long books. Reading researcher Olivia Brennan tested this idea with records from a library app in Dublin, Ireland, that tracks how far users get in both e-books and audiobooks. For each range of book lengths, she calculated the share of borrowers who finished the book. Brennan found that the assumption held only for the longest books: ______

data.title: Share of Library App Borrowers Who Finished a Book, by Format and Length

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the statement?

choices.A: audiobook borrowers finished books in every length range at a lower rate than e-book borrowers did.
choices.B: for books over 500 pages, only 41 percent of e-book borrowers and 29 percent of audiobook borrowers finished.
choices.C: the share of borrowers finishing fell as books got longer for both e-books and audiobooks.
choices.D: audiobook borrowers finished at equal or higher rates than e-book borrowers for books up to 500 pages, but at a much lower rate for books over 500 pages.

explanation.why: The statement says the assumption (that listeners give up more readily) held only for the longest books, so the choice must show both halves: no audiobook disadvantage for shorter books and a clear one for the longest. For the first three rows the audiobook rate is higher (74 vs. 71, 65 vs. 63, 54 vs. 52); for books over 500 pages it is much lower (29 vs. 41).
explanation.A: Incorrect. This misreads the table: for the three shorter ranges, audiobook borrowers finished at a slightly higher rate, not a lower one.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This shows the longest books only, so it supports the assumption without showing that it failed for shorter books, which "only" requires.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is true, but it describes length alone and never compares the two formats, which is what the assumption is about.
explanation.D: Correct. This shows that audiobooks matched or beat e-books up to 500 pages and fell far behind only for the longest books, exactly what the statement needs.
